title: Lipidomics at the Frontier of Possibility: Transformative Potential and Methodological Challenges in Biomedical Research
content: This work provides a comprehensive analysis of the current state and future prospects of lipidomics. Lipidomics is a critical tool in systems biology and translational medicine. The study substantiates the concept that lipidomics possesses high transformative potential. This potential is necessary for deciphering the pathogenesis of complex diseases and discovering new biomarkers. The full practical realization of this potential is possible only by overcoming analytical barriers and systematically integrating with other omics technologies. The fundamental role of lipids in cellular processes is highlighted. The necessity of a systemic approach to their identification is demonstrated. The work is divided into three logical blocks. The first block examines the methodological foundations of mass spectrometry ("shotgun" lipidomics, LC-MS/MS, MALDI-MSI, IM-MS) and analyzes their limitations in detail. Particular attention is paid to the phenomenon of in-source fragmentation. This leads to the generation of spectral artifacts and erroneous lipid species annotation. Challenges related to the separation of structural and stereoisomers are also discussed. The second block reveals the clinical potential of lipidomics. Examples of cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and oncological pathologies are considered. The third block is devoted to multi-omics integration and the application of artificial intelligence methods. These are necessary for moving from observational correlations to causal mechanisms. Priority directions for future research are formulated. Protocol standardization and the implementation of high-resolution analytical methods for clinical practice are discussed.
